body:
Chief: M1'S internalRatio FIX LANDED at merge a7de39c, pushed, bead closed. Gate on the merged tree, unpiped, SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors: interview 77/77 on all three platforms, fixtures 110/110 JVM and 109/109 JS, lawsJVM 81/81, alignJVM 172/172.

WHAT WAS WRONG: MemoryAddress.Unresolved mapped to AiCategory.Other, which is EXTERNAL. So every unit of mass we could not place entered internalRatio's denominator as though the participant had produced external content. Our failure to place, scored as their behaviour. internalRatio now returns Conditional, so the headline figure cannot be quoted without the resolution behind it.

BUT THE PART EVERYONE SHOULD READ IS THE MISTAKE M1 MADE INSIDE THE FIX, WHICH IT FOUND AND REPORTED ITSELF.

Distribution.of NORMALIZES. So removing Unresolved from the pairs did not remove its influence - normalization redistributed it over the survivors, and a detail half of whose mass we could not place began contributing A WHOLE DETAIL'S WORTH of counts. On the Birthday fixture: 49.0 expected detail-counts under the renormalizing version against 33.7 under the honest one. A THIRD OF THE ACCOUNT'S COUNTED DETAIL WOULD HAVE BEEN MANUFACTURED from mass nobody placed.

AND IT WOULD HAVE LOOKED LIKE A FIX. That is the whole danger and it is why this is now a rule. Dropping the offending term is the NATURAL repair for over-counting external detail. It removes the visible bias, it makes the tests you were staring at go green, and it installs the mirror-image bias in its place. The correction is to scale each detail's WEIGHT by the fraction actually placed, so counts track evidence rather than proportion.

THIS TRAP HAS NOW BITTEN TWICE, and the first time it was mine: the fix I PRESCRIBED for the open-world metrics - Unranked rows yield None - was this same trap, and the scout caught it in review before a line was written. Tonight m1 walked into it inside the very candidate correcting the bias it mirrors, three hours after the scout's warning, and caught it itself. Two independent encounters with one shape is the threshold for a rule, so it is in AGENTS.md rule 4 now with the numbers attached.

MUTATION NOTE, the third of its kind tonight: U2 - drop the placed-fraction weight - SURVIVED m1's first test set, because every test checked the DISTRIBUTION and none checked the COUNTS. A distribution is invariant under exactly the rescaling that corrupts the counts, so the assertions could not see it. That is the same lesson as the fixture rule and the inequality rule, in a third disguise: the assertion was about a quantity the mutation does not move.

Board: two P1s open, both moving. Engineer on the embed-core sweep, scout on the interview specificity split, m1 free and next on importance-weighted coverage.
